title: Ajapsandali
skill: Every vegetable diced evenly and timed

notes.text: Brown the eggplant in three batches, and use the largest pot you have.

move.title: Five vegetables, three sizes
move.body: Ajapsandali is a Georgian summer stew of eggplant, peppers, potato, tomato, and onion, finished with a big handful of herbs. Each vegetable is diced to the size that lets it finish with the others. This is the unit's mastery week: you'll cut everything yourself and time how long the knife work takes.

why.title: Size by cooking time
why.body: Potato stays firm the longest, so it's cut smallest, ½ inch. Eggplant and peppers soften fast, so they're cut bigger, ¾ inch, to keep their shape. Onion and tomato are meant to melt into the sauce, so ½ inch is plenty. Different sizes, one finish.

why.title: Salt the eggplant first
why.body: Salt draws water out of eggplant. Drier cubes brown in the oil instead of soaking it up, and hold together in the stew.

why.title: Potatoes wait in water
why.body: Cut potatoes turn gray-brown in the air. A bowl of cold water keeps them white until they go in the pot.

why.title: Brown, then simmer
why.body: Browning the eggplant and onions before anything else gives the stew its deep, sweet flavor. Once the tomatoes go in, nothing browns anymore; it only simmers.

why.title: Herbs and garlic at the end
why.body: Raw garlic and fresh herbs stirred in off the heat stay sharp and green. Ten minutes of resting lets them flavor the whole pot without cooking away.

wrong.sign: The eggplant soaked up all the oil and looks dry
wrong.fix: Keep cooking; it will release some of the oil as it browns. Next time, salt it longer and pat it drier.

wrong.sign: The potatoes are still hard when everything else is soft
wrong.fix: They were cut too big. Keep simmering, covered, until a cube squashes easily.
Simmer it with the lid off for the last 10 minutes.

wrong.sign: The eggplant fell apart into mush
wrong.fix: It was cut too small or stirred too hard. Fold gently from the bottom after it goes back in.

quiz.q: Why are the potatoes cut smaller than the eggplant?
quiz.explain: Size by cooking time, so everything finishes together.

quiz.q: Why salt the eggplant before cooking?
choices: To draw out water so it browns

quiz.q: Why do the cut potatoes wait in water?
When do the garlic and herbs go in?
choices: At the end, off the heat

steps.text: Wash all the vegetables and set out the board, the knife, and the bowls. Note the time: the knife work, from the eggplant to the garlic, is this week's mastery check.
steps.tip: Even first, fast second. A neat dice in 25 minutes beats a ragged one in 15.

steps.text: Trim the ends off the eggplant. Cut it into ¾-inch slices, the slices into ¾-inch strips, and the strips into ¾-inch cubes. Toss them in the colander with the vegetables' salt and set the colander in the sink.
steps.look: Cubes about ¾ inch, close to the same size.

steps.text: Fill the medium bowl with cold water. Peel the potatoes, cut a thin slice off one side so each sits flat, and cut them into ½-inch planks, sticks, and cubes. Drop the cubes into the water as you go.
steps.look: ½-inch cubes, smaller than the eggplant.

steps.text: Halve and peel the onions, leaving the root on, and dice them into ½-inch pieces. Put them in the large bowl.
Cut the sides off the peppers' cores, lay them skin side down, and cut them into ¾-inch squares. If you're using the jalapeño, seed it and dice it fine. Add both to the onion.
steps.tip: Wash your hands with soap right after cutting the jalapeño.

steps.text: Core the tomatoes and cut them into ½-inch pieces. Keep them, with their juice, in a separate pile on the board.
Mince the garlic and put it in the small bowl. Chop the cilantro and basil and add them to the garlic. Check the time: that's your knife-work time for this week.
Spread the eggplant on the towel and pat it dry with paper towels, pressing firmly.

Heat 4 tablespoons of the oil in the large pot over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the eggplant and cook, turning now and then, until browned on several sides. Lift it out onto the plate with the slotted spoon.
Turn the heat to medium and add the rest of the oil, the onions, and the peppers. Cook, stirring, until the onion is soft and golden.

Drain the potatoes and add them with the paprika, the stew's salt, and the pepper. Stir for a minute, then add the tomatoes, the water, and the eggplant. Bring it to a simmer, cover, and turn the heat to low. Stir gently from the bottom every 10 minutes.
steps.look: A potato cube squashes easily against the pot, and the eggplant still holds its shape.

steps.text: Turn off the heat. Gently stir in the garlic and herbs, cover, and let the stew rest. Taste and add salt a pinch at a time if it needs it.
Serve it warm or at room temperature.
steps.tip: It tastes even better the next day. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
